newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber off sharply on weak cash market, stops.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber off sharply on weak cash market, stops.

text.p: CME lumber futures were sharply lower at mid-morning as selling linked to a weak cash market helped to trigger stops, floor sources said.
They noted Saul Stone was a featured seller.
Spruce was selling in the cash market at $355 to $360 per thousand board foot area, which was down from the official Random Lengths quote of $362 late last week, dealers said.
At 1050 CDT, lumber stood $5.90 to the $10.00 per tbf limit lower with July off $7.30 at $367.20 and September off $9.00 at $362.30 per tbf.
